title: EvidenceEnvelope
description: The seller's delivery package. `artifact_hash` is the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical serialization of `statement`, and is the exact value recorded on chain by submitDelivery (there, 0x-prefixed). Because the canonical bytes are what is hashed, `sha256sum` over the stored canonical statement reproduces the on-chain value with no Sinetti tooling. See docs/evidence.md.

sha256.description: SHA-256 as 64 lowercase hex characters, with no 0x prefix

artifact_ref.description: Where the delivered files can be fetched. Integrity comes from the per-file digests in statement.subject, never from this reference.

artifact_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical serialization of `statement`. Must equal the deal's on-chain evidenceHash.

logs_ref.description: Where the test log can be fetched. Its integrity is statement.predicate.logs_hash.

statement.description: in-toto Statement v1 shape, copied not imported. The subject list is per-file: an archive is never hashed, because archive bytes vary run to run with entry order, timestamps and compression level.

subject.description: Every delivered file, each with its own digest, sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of `name` ascending. UTF-8 byte order is specified because array order is preserved by RFC 8785 rather than imposed by it, so two producers that disagree about the order compute different artifact_hash values for byte-identical deliveries. It is what Python `sorted`, Go and Rust give by default; JavaScript's `<` on strings is UTF-16 code-unit order and differs whenever a supplementary-plane character is compared against one in U+E000-U+FFFF.

name.description: POSIX path relative to the delivery root

predicate.description: The fields docs/evidence.md checks. They sit inside the statement so the commitment covers them: a value outside the hashed statement could be edited without changing artifact_hash.

runtime_hash.description: Fingerprint of the agreed execution environment

logs_hash.description: SHA-256 of the test log content at logs_ref
